o: We maintain videos keyed by ID, counters for views/likes/dislikes, and must always allocate the smallest free ID, reusing IDs after deletion. All methods must first check existence and gracefully return -1-type sentinels otherwise. With up to 1e5 operations and total video length 1e5, a hash map plus a min-heap (or ordered set) of freed IDs gives O(log n) allocation. Example 1 shows reuse of ID 0 after removal, and watch clipping the end minute to the video length.
k: A min-heap of deleted IDs plus a next-fresh-ID counter yields smallest-available allocation.
Every operation except upload needs an existence check on the ID.
watch returns video[startMinute .. min(endMinute, len-1)] inclusive and increments views only when the video exists.

a.n: Approach 1: Hash map + min-heap of free IDs
a.i: Store each live video's string and counters in dictionaries. On upload, pop the smallest freed ID from the heap, or take a brand-new ID if the heap is empty. On remove, delete the entry and push the ID back. All other operations are O(1) lookups guarded by existence checks.
s: Init maps for video/likes/dislikes/views, an empty min-heap, and nextId = 0.
upload: take heap top if available else nextId++, store video, return ID.
remove/watch/like/dislike/getters: check membership first; watch slices to min(endMinute, len-1) and bumps views.
remove pushes the ID onto the min-heap for reuse.
a.t: O(log n) per upload/remove due to heap ops; O(1) or O(slice length) for others.
a.sp: O(total video length + number of live videos).

w: A TreeSet/sorted container of free IDs works equally well. Common pitfalls: incrementing views on nonexistent videos, off-by-one on the inclusive end minute, and forgetting ID reuse. Follow-ups might ask for LRU caching of hot videos or range-view analytics.
